patterns_found.visual_evidence: The desktop sketch shows a horizontal row of top navigation items beneath the hero/header area, suggesting primary nav links that may expose deeper site sections. The grouped nav structure implies possible submenu behavior on hover or click.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: If implemented as a multi-level site nav, top-level items would reveal submenus on hover and click/focus, with active-state indication for the current section.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly draw submenu panels or carets, so these may also be simple links rather than dropdowns.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The desktop layout has a clearly separated horizontal navigation strip near the top, spanning the page width, which is a common pattern for a nav bar intended to remain available while reading long article content below.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: If sticky, the nav bar should pin to the top after scroll and preserve access to section/site navigation while the long content body is read.
patterns_found.ambiguities: No explicit fixed-position cue is drawn; this is inferred from the long-scroll article layout rather than directly shown.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches depict long vertically scrolling content pages with substantial article text, making a return-to-top affordance a likely implied interaction for usability even though no explicit button is drawn.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: A button would appear after the user scrolls down and return them smoothly to the top/header area when activated.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The control is not explicitly sketched, so this is a usability inference rather than a directly depicted component.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches include clusters of small square social/media-style icons in the lower profile/contact card area. These commonly trigger share dialogs, enlarged media, or contact overlays rather than simple inline changes.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: If icons open overlays such as share/contact/media dialogs, the modal should trap focus, support escape/close actions, and return focus to the triggering icon.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The icons may simply be outbound links with no JS at all; the sketch does not specify overlay behavior.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Any interactive overlay or disclosure behavior implied by navigation and icon-triggered panels would require managed keyboard focus. This is especially relevant if desktop nav uses dropdowns or if social/contact actions open dialogs.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Programmatic focus should move into opened menus/dialogs and return to the trigger on close; hidden panels should be removed from tab order.
patterns_found.ambiguities: This depends on whether the inferred dropdown/modal behaviors are actually implemented.

sketch_notes: The sketches primarily depict a content-heavy informational page with image blocks, navigation rows, article text, and a footer/profile card with social icons. Very little explicit JavaScript is drawn; most of the page could be implemented statically. The strongest implied JS needs come from desktop navigation behavior and any overlay/share interactions attached to icon clusters. Mobile appears especially light on explicit interaction patterns, with no clearly drawn hamburger, forms, tabs, or accordions.
